title: Each tab keeps its own in-memory copy and saves the whole list, so a second tab erases the first tab's recipes
evidence: Driven with two pages in one browser context, both loaded empty. Tab 1 adds FromTab1, Tab 2 adds FromTab2. localStorage afterwards: [{"id":...,"name":"FromTab2","minutes":6}]. There is no 'storage' event listener and no re-read before save (app.js:3 reads once).
failing_case: Open the app in two tabs, add a recipe in each: the recipe added first is gone after the second save, and no message appears. Delete in a stale tab likewise resurrects or removes the wrong set.
remediation: Re-read storage (loadRecipes) immediately before each mutation and save, or listen for the 'storage' event and re-render; one writer per record.

quote: // storage blocked or corrupt: start empty; app.js tells the user
title: Corrupt or blocked storage loads as an empty list with no message, and the next save overwrites the stored data; the comment says app.js tells the user, and it does not
evidence: Driven in Chromium. localStorage 'recipes' set to '{bad', page reloaded: list shows 'No recipes yet. Add your first one above.' and #status is ''. grep of app.js: nothing reads a load failure; loadRecipes returns only an array, so app.js cannot tell 'empty' from 'failed'. The next saveRecipes call overwrites the key. Same silent path for a valid array whose entries fail the name test at store.js:7.
failing_case: A user's saved list is damaged (truncated write, manual edit, another version). They open the app, see the friendly empty state, add one recipe: saveRecipes writes a one-item list over the old value. The old text is gone with no warning and no chance to export it. If storage is blocked, the user sees an empty list, with no hint that nothing will persist, until their first save fails.
remediation: Return {list, error} (or throw) from loadRecipes; when it reports corrupt or blocked, show a message in #status, keep the raw string (for example under 'recipes.bak') before any overwrite, and offer the recovery next step.

title: Delete ignores the result of saveRecipes and reports 'Deleted' even when nothing was persisted
evidence: Driven: with Storage.prototype.setItem made to throw, clicking Delete shows status 'Deleted “...”.' The add path at app.js:24 checks the boolean; the delete path drops it.
failing_case: Storage is full or blocked. The user deletes a recipe, sees 'Deleted', reloads, and the recipe is back. The user was told something that did not happen.
remediation: Branch on the saveRecipes result as the add handler does: on false, say the deletion could not be saved and will be undone on reload (or roll back the in-memory list).

title: After a keyboard delete the focused button is destroyed by innerHTML and focus drops to body
evidence: Driven: focused the first Delete button, pressed Enter, accepted the confirm; document.activeElement.tagName was BODY. render() at app.js:10 replaces the whole list. Status is announced by role=status, but keyboard position is lost (WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order, AA).
failing_case: A keyboard or switch user deletes one of ten recipes; focus restarts at the top of the document and they must tab through the form again to reach the next Delete.
remediation: After render, move focus to the next row's Delete button (or the previous one, or the 'Your recipes' heading when the list is empty).

quote: return Array.isArray(data) ? data.filter((r) => r && typeof r.name === "string") : [];
title: loadRecipes validates only name; records without id or with a non-number minutes give NaN or concatenated totals and an undeletable row
evidence: Driven. Stored [{name:'Soup',minutes:20},{name:7,minutes:9},{name:'Stew',minutes:'30'}] (no ids, no schema version). List renders. Adding 'Pie' (10) shows 'Total cooking time: 203010 minutes.' (string concatenation from totalMinutes at store.js:23). Clicking Delete on 'Soup' throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading name)' from describe(r) at app.js:33 because x.id === 'undefined' never matches; the row stays. The record with name 7 is silently dropped and erased by the next save. The comment at app.js:14 ('never null here') is false for these records.
failing_case: A list saved by an earlier version without ids (or with minutes saved as strings) is loaded: the status line reports a wrong total, Delete does nothing but throw, and records with a non-string name disappear permanently on the next save.
remediation: Normalise at the load boundary: require a string id (assign newId() when missing), coerce minutes with Number and reject non-finite values, and keep a 'v' field on the saved shape with a migration.
